web.config.gateways_hint: Gateways ghostline connects to. asterisk — Asterisk (FreePBX or plain) with chan_quectel / chan_dongle modems, over AMI; yeastar — AMI; goip — SMTP and HTTP.
web.config.hint.general: sms — SMS only; full — also calls: journal, recordings, transcription. Languages: empty — the default one.
web.config.hint.telegram: Empty token: Telegram is off. Common chats for lines without their own. An SMS is sent from a chat with two lines (number, text) if the chat serves one line, three (line, number, text) if several. Chat ids — comma separated.
web.config.hint.web: Empty user and password — no authentication. The port applies after a restart.
web.config.hint.calls: Only for mode full. Recordings: the HTTP address of /var/spool/asterisk/monitor on the PBX, or that directory shared with the PBX (wins). CDR SQLite: the file Asterisk writes with cdr_sqlite3_custom, instead of the MySQL below.
web.config.hint.cdr_db: MySQL of the PBX (asteriskcdrdb); a user with SELECT on cdr is enough.
web.config.hint.transcribe: Any OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions. The prompt — names and terms that are often misrecognized; avoid similar-sounding words.
web.config.hint.goip: Built-in SMTP server for GoIP gateways that deliver SMS by e-mail.
web.config.hint.monitor: Asterisk gateways with monitoring on are polled once a minute: registration, operator, network type, signal of every modem. A line without network for this many minutes gets a message in its chats and topic, and another when it is back; 0: no messages. The AMI user needs "reporting" in "write".
web.field.logger.file: Also write SMS and calls to /var/log/ghostline (text files for other systems)
web.field.monitor.alert_minutes: Alert after no network for, min

web.field.lines.calls.chat_ids: Telegram chats for calls only (empty — the line's)

web.config.hint.ntfy: Self-hosted push (ntfy server). Empty address: off. Lines go to their own topic (ntfy topic of the line) or to the common topic. A message written in the topic in the ntfy app is sent as an SMS: two lines (number, text) if the topic serves one line, three (line, number, text) if several.
tg.help.intro: ghostline connects the SIM lines of your gateway or PBX with this chat. Incoming SMS come here.
tg.help.sms.one:
Send an SMS from the line {0}: two lines, the number and the text: 
+79001234567
Hello!
tg.help.sms.many:
Send an SMS: three lines, the line, the number and the text: 
{0}
+79001234567
Hello!
Lines: {1}
tg.sms.wrong.one: This doesn't look like an SMS to send. To send from the line {0} write two lines: the recipient's number and the text. /help — more
tg.sms.wrong.many: This doesn't look like an SMS to send. Write three lines: the line, the recipient's number and the text. Lines: {0} /help — more
web.field.ntfy.topic: Common topic (for lines without their own)
web.config.hint.clients: Where notifications go and where SMS can be sent from. Telegram and ntfy are optional: a client that is not here is off. A line can have its own chats and topic (Lines → line → Clients).
web.config.hint.line_clients: Clients of this line: notifications go only to the ones listed here. Empty chats / topic inside a client: the common ones.
web.config.hint.line_telegram: Telegram chats of this line (SMS and calls). Empty: the common chats.
web.config.hint.line_ntfy: ntfy topic of this line. Empty: the common topic.
web.config.hint.line_calls: What to send for calls on this line (mode full only).
web.config.remove_client_confirm: Remove {0}? Notifications will not be sent there.
web.config.hint.line_clients_unset: Not set: the line goes to every client that is on, with the common chats and topic. Add a client to choose explicitly.
web.config.lines_hint: SIM lines. The name is used in the bot and the interface. On an Asterisk gateway the line is one of its modems, on yeastar / goip a port. Own chats and topic (Clients) are optional: without them the line uses the common ones. A line on the managed Asterisk can have a phone.
web.config.hint.managed: ghostline writes the PJSIP, dialplan and modem files of this Asterisk into conf_dir (a directory shared with it; Asterisk sees it as asterisk_dir) and reloads them over AMI on every save. Phones connect over TLS; a relative certificate path is inside conf_dir.
web.config.hint.modems: The modems of this Asterisk, as named in FreePBX's quectel.conf / dongle.conf: ghostline only needs the name and the driver. Added and removed at once.
web.config.hint.modems_managed: The modems of this Asterisk: ghostline writes their ports into quectel_ghostline.conf / dongle_ghostline.conf. Added and removed at once; the driver reloads after the calls on it end. The live state is on the Status tab.
web.config.hint.phone: The SIP phone of this line: the SIM rings it, and it calls out through the SIM. Empty extension: no phone. Registration is on the Status tab.
web.pbx.modem.none_freepbx: No modems: add the ones FreePBX has (their names in quectel.conf / dongle.conf).
web.pbx.modem.hint_freepbx: The name as in FreePBX's quectel.conf / dongle.conf.
web.pbx.usb.title: USB modems on the host not used yet
web.config.hint.logger: The system log (System tab, journald, /var/log/ghostline/system-*.log, 14 days) keeps entries of this level and more severe: errors < warnings < info < debug. The SMS and calls journal (PBX tab) is read from the database and does not need the text files.
